introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics With Statistics, Paper 3 (0770/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Time allowed: THREE HOURS.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae and tables produced by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Electronic calculators may be used. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A sample of 60 pupils is taken from a school; their masses, in kg, are measured and recorded in a frequency table as shown below.

| Mass | 16 - 20 | 21 - 25 | 26 - 30 | 31 - 35 | 36 - 40 | 41 - 45 | 46 - 50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of pupils | 5 | 10 | 18 | 12 | 8 | 4 | 3 |

Calculate, to one decimal place, the
incertitudes: Question 2 : le sujet ne dit pas que les masses sont arrondies au kg le plus proche ; c'est l'hypothèse retenue (classes 16 - 20 = $15.5 \le x < 20.5$, frontières 15.5, 20.5, ..., 50.5), comme pour tout tableau de données groupées de ce type. Avec ces frontières, $Q_1 = 25.5$ et $Q_3 = 35.5$ tombent exactement sur des frontières de classe.

Question 2 (c) : le sujet demande de tracer la courbe des fréquences cumulées ; le corrigé décrit le tracé et donne les points ; l'écart interquartile est calculé par interpolation linéaire (valeur exacte 10.0 kg, une lecture graphique correcte donne environ 10 kg). Le sujet n'imprime pas de figure.
Question 2 : les points imprimés par partie, 4, 3 et 6, totalisent 13 ; recopiés tels quels.

questions.corrige_markdown:
$n = 60$, so the median is the $\dfrac{n}{2} = 30$th value. The cumulative frequencies at the upper class boundaries are $5, 15, 33, 45, 53, 57, 60$, so the median lies in the class $26 - 30$ (boundaries $25.5$ to $30.5$): below $25.5$ there are $15$ pupils, below $30.5$ there are $33$.

Interpolating linearly inside the class (lower boundary $L = 25.5$, class frequency $f_m = 18$, class width $c = 5$, cumulative frequency before the class $F = 15$):

$$\text{Median} = L + \frac{\frac{n}{2} - F}{f_m} \times c = 25.5 + \frac{30 - 15}{18} \times 5 = 25.5 + 4.1667 = 29.6667$$

**Median mass $\approx 29.7$ kg.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a cumulative frequency curve for the data and use it to estimate the interquartile range.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Cumulative frequency table.** Because the masses are rounded to the nearest kg, a cumulative frequency is plotted against the **upper class boundary**, starting at $(15.5, 0)$.

| Upper boundary, $x$ (kg) | 15.5 | 20.5 | 25.5 | 30.5 | 35.5 | 40.5 | 45.5 | 50.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | 0 | 5 | 15 | 33 | 45 | 53 | 57 | 60 |

**Drawing.** Horizontal axis: mass $x$ in kg from 15.5 to 50.5 (for example 2 cm for 5 kg); vertical axis: cumulative frequency from 0 to 60 (for example 2 cm for 10 pupils). Plot the eight points and join them with a smooth S-shaped curve (an ogive). Label both axes. The curve is steepest between $x = 25.5$ and $x = 30.5$, where the class frequency (18) is largest.

**Reading the quartiles.**

- Lower quartile: cumulative frequency $\dfrac{n}{4} = 15$. Read across from $15$ to the curve, then down: $Q_1 = 25.5$ kg (the point $(25.5, 15)$ is exactly on the curve).
- Upper quartile: cumulative frequency $\dfrac{3n}{4} = 45$. Read across from $45$ to the curve, then down: $Q_3 = 35.5$ kg (the point $(35.5, 45)$ is exactly on the curve).

$$\text{Interquartile range} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 35.5 - 25.5 = 10.0$$

**Interquartile range $\approx 10.0$ kg.** (The median can be read in the same way at cumulative frequency $30$: about $29.7$ kg, as in part (b).)
